headline: Southborough received a nearly $3.9 million culvert grant, approved a Neary school architect contract, and appointed a new student support services director.
synopsis: The Select Board announced nearly $3.9 million in state culvert grant funding that will allow Southborough to avoid previously authorized borrowing, while also approving an architect contract for the Neary school feasibility study. The Southborough School Committee voted unanimously to hire Daniel Mazur as the district's Director of Student Support Services. Town committees also adjusted capital requests ahead of the June 30 Community Preservation Act deadline, with the Trails Committee scaling back its application to focus solely on a trail bridge and the Golf Committee examining irrigation costs approaching $1 million. In land use, the Conservation Commission reviewed a 32-unit Chapter 40B proposal on Turnpike Road, and the Planning Board recommended a conditional occupancy permit for 200 Turnpike Road.

highlights.title: State culvert grant eliminates need for town borrowing
highlights.why: Southborough was awarded $3,891,000 from the state culvert program, allowing the town to eventually rescind $3.9 million in borrowing previously authorized by Town Meeting.

highlights.title: Architect contract approved for Neary school study
highlights.why: The Select Board approved a contract with Tappe Architects to evaluate both options approved by Town Meeting for the Neary Elementary School project.

highlights.title: Daniel Mazur appointed Director of Student Support Services
highlights.why: The School Committee voted 5-0 to confirm Daniel Mazur to oversee Southborough K-8 student support services, targeting a July 1 start date.

highlights.title: Conservation Commission reviews 32-unit 40B development
highlights.why: The commission reviewed wetland impacts and vernal pool wildlife passages for a 32-unit rental townhouse project proposed at 250 Turnpike Road, continuing the hearing to June 25.

highlights.title: Trails Committee drops boardwalk to seek bridge-only CPA funds
highlights.why: With combined project estimates reaching $630,000, the committee decided to seek Community Preservation Act funds only for a $410,000 footbridge ahead of the June 30 deadline.

highlights.title: Golf course irrigation project estimates climb near $1 million
highlights.why: The Golf Committee evaluated funding strategies and potential phasing as rising equipment and materials costs doubled the irrigation project's original $500,000 estimate.
